case_name: SRL-2018 Remote Desktop Server RD-04 — Memory Forensics (Primary C2 Pivot)
description: Volatility3 memory analysis. 30 LOTL processes + code injection in 33 processes. The most operationally active compromised host in SRL-2018 corpus. 30 simultaneous LOTL processes is the signature of an active C2 framework with multiple concurrent beacons. Primary attacker pivot post-lateral-movement.
devil_advocate: High LOTL counts on RD servers can reflect automated administration scripts. PowerShell remoting with multiple sessions can produce high cmd/powershell counts.

artifacts.content: vol3 windows.pslist LOLBAS: 30 living-off-the-land processes detected simultaneously. Highest LOTL count in entire SRL-2018 corpus. Cobalt Strike beacon pattern: multiple short-lived rundll32.exe instances spawned by powershell.exe parent (confirmed in RD-02 transcript analysis).
forensic_anomalies: 30 simultaneous LOTL processes is 15x the maximum expected for legitimate admin activity — no legitimate use case produces this count
Pattern matches Cobalt Strike beacon with sleep jitter spawning multiple rundll32.exe shellcode hosts in rotation — each short-lived process executes one C2 task then exits
Highest LOTL count in corpus (RD04: 30 > RD01: 12 > ADMIN: 2 > WKSTN04: 2) identifies RD-04 as primary operational C2 base

artifacts.content: vol3 windows.malfind: code injection in 33 processes (PIDs: 8b, 4896, ac, 10, a4 and 28 others). 33 injected processes — the broadest injection footprint among all servers except RD-05.
forensic_anomalies: 33 injected processes with 30 active LOTL indicates nearly every LOLBAS process is a shellcode container — systematic framework deployment, not selective targeting
Breadth of injection (33 processes) suggests the attacker established redundant persistence to survive process termination by defenders
Combined LOTL (30) + injection (33) count indicates RD-04 was the attacker's primary working environment for extended operations

artifacts.content: RD-04 as C2 pivot: 30 active beacon processes at acquisition time indicates continuous external communication. Attack timeline: admin compromised (Jul 2018) -> AV disabled -> RD-04 established as primary C2 -> lateral spread to RD-01/03/05/06 and WKSTN-04.
forensic_anomalies: Primary C2 pivot identification changes incident narrative: the attacker operated primarily from RD-04, not the admin server
30 concurrent beacons provides high resilience against partial cleanup — killing some processes does not disrupt C2 continuity
RD-04 connectivity to all RD servers and WKSTN via RDP explains the uniform injection pattern across the corpus

peirce_chain.firstness: RD server in network — highest RDP connectivity to other servers and workstations
peirce_chain.secondness: 30 LOTL + 33 code injection — most operationally active compromised host in corpus
peirce_chain.thirdness: 30 concurrent beacons identifies RD-04 as primary C2 pivot. Attacker conducted extended operations from this host, using it to spread to all other RD servers and WKSTN-04. Highest persistence value to attacker.

_consolidation: VIGÍA-REAL. vol3 RD04-001. Bundle: results/srl2018/RD04-001_bundle.json. PRIMARY C2 PIVOT identification — highest forensic value in SRL-2018 memory corpus.
